# smtpfast_link_domain (Resource)

A custom link domain: your own hostname, such as `links.example.com`, for the open pixel, tracked links and unsubscribe links in email from your domain, instead of `smtpfa.st`. Publish the CNAME record (`hostname` pointing at `cname_target`) with your DNS provider; the link domain turns `active` once SMTPfast sees it and issues the certificate, usually within minutes. On Cloudflare, keep the record DNS only (not proxied).

The hostname must be a subdomain of a verified sending domain on the team, one link domain per sending domain. Link domains are on paid plans.

Terraform does not wait for `active`: the CNAME record usually depends on this resource, so both are created in the same apply and `status` updates on the next refresh.

Needs a provider API key with the `domain:read` and `domain:write` scopes, from an owner or admin.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Serve open tracking, click tracking and unsubscribe links from your own
# hostname, and publish its CNAME record to Cloudflare in the same apply.
# Swap cloudflare_record for aws_route53_record, etc. as needed.
#
# The hostname must be a subdomain of a verified sending domain on the team.

resource "smtpfast_link_domain" "links" {
  hostname = "links.example.com"
}

resource "cloudflare_record" "smtpfast_links" {
  zone_id = var.cloudflare_zone_id
  type    = "CNAME"
  name    = smtpfast_link_domain.links.hostname
  content = smtpfast_link_domain.links.cname_target
  proxied = false # DNS only: SMTPfast issues the certificate for the hostname
}

output "link_domain_status" {
  # pending until the CNAME record is seen and the certificate is issued,
  # usually within minutes; refresh to see active.
  value = smtpfast_link_domain.links.status
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hostname` (String) The link hostname, e.g. `links.example.com`, in lowercase and without a trailing dot (the form the API stores). It must be a subdomain of a verified sending domain on the team. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `cname_target` (String) Where the CNAME record must point, such as `links.smtpfa.st`. Use it with `hostname` in your DNS provider's record resource.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `dns_records` (Attributes List) Records to publish: the required CNAME first, then any optional TXT record Cloudflare offers to activate the hostname before the CNAME is live. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dns_records))
- `domain` (String) The sending domain the hostname sits under.
- `domain_id` (String) ID of the sending domain the hostname sits under.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the link domain.
- `last_error` (String) Why the link domain is not active yet, when known.
- `ssl_status` (String) Certificate status as Cloudflare reports it, for troubleshooting.
- `status` (String) `pending` until the CNAME record is seen and the certificate is issued, then `active`. `failed` means it will not become active without a change on your side; `last_error` says why. Mail uses the link domain only while it is `active`.
- `verified_at` (String) When the link domain first became active (RFC 3339), or null.

<a id="nestedatt--dns_records"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dns_records`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) Record name.
- `purpose` (String) What the record is for.
- `required` (Boolean) Whether the record is required. The CNAME is; a TXT record is optional.
- `status` (String) `pending` while the link domain is not active. Once it is, the CNAME is `verified` (keep it: certificate renewals need it) and a TXT record is `not_needed`.
- `type` (String) Record type: `CNAME` or `TXT`.
- `value` (String) Record value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by link domain id.
terraform import smtpfast_link_domain.links ld_abc123
```
